column3: “Before the face of” is rendered “in the presence of.”
Close to the Greek; the first line is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“His father”); “marveling” is rendered “amazed.”
NASB renders “spoken against” as “to be opposed” and “falling and rising up” as “fall and rise.”
NASB renders “go through” as “pierce” and “so that” as “to the end that.”
NASB restructures the verse; “years great” is rendered “advanced in years.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to the age of”), adding “then as” and “never.”
NASB follows the critical text (“God,” “of Jerusalem”); “giving praise” is rendered “giving thanks.”
NASB follows the critical text; “town” is rendered “city.”
NASB follows the critical text (no “in spirit”); “being filled with wisdom” is rendered “increasing in wisdom.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“went up”) and adds “there.”
NASB follows the critical text (“His parents”); “not knew” is rendered “were unaware of it.”
NASB renders “company” as “caravan.”
NASB follows the critical text (“looking for”).
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “Child” as “Son” and “distressing” as “anxiously.”
NASB renders “in the things of My Father” as “in My Father’s house”; the Greek may also mean “about My Father’s business.”
“Declaration” is rendered “statement.”
NASB follows the critical text without “these”; “declarations” is rendered “things.”
NASB renders “was continuing to advance” as “kept increasing.”
